question: Which GT24 channels can be signed and normalized canonically from independent source evidence, with which masses, and how do collection phases, days and exo conditions map?
scope: All 2421 Parsed recordings in 25 phase/subject folders; metadata, README and existing audits only. No GT24 time series read by this task.

collection_phases.text: Phase1And2: data phase 1 (BT01-BT12, unpowered all tasks + heuristic controller some tasks) and data phase 2 (BT13-BT17, preliminary model, all powered). Phase3: BT01, BT02, BT13 returned + BT18-BT24, all powered.

answer.signs: Hip +1, knee -1, ankle +1 for sagittal angles, velocities, net/biological/assistance moments (powers unchanged). Ankle: no negation (GT24-C02). Frontal/transverse: source sign kept.
answer.source_divisor: Not established. Re-reading the GT24-C02 lever-arm slopes (6 trials) with the externally calibrated GT23-C04 lever bias (0.9942) fits the worn model mass (person + exoskeleton) in 6/6 and body mass in 1/6 (BT24 folder, by coincidence of values); this assumes the GT23 bias transfers to GT24. With a free bias the slopes cannot separate worn from body mass. the BT24 folder fits its Statics model mass (74.96 kg, BT18's README row), not BT24's README 84.84 kg. Exact per-trial divisors need the probe (E1 identity).
answer.normalization_basis: Queued: D-GT24-C01-1 (participant body mass vs worn mass vs withhold), held until the divisor probe reports. It sets a convention for exoskeleton datasets, so José decides.
answer.masses: README w/ exo exceeds w/o exo by 6.12-7.81 kg (ratio 1.065-1.131) in all 31 rows.
answer.phase_day_exo: Collection from the zip (never from subject IDs); exo state from the _on/_off/_hilo suffix; no no-exoskeleton trials exist; day bound only through an exact model-mass match (Phase3 Statics, or the E1 divisor for Phase1And2).

BT01, BT02 and BT13 occur in both with different masses and models; never merge or infer collection from the ID. Within Phase1And2, README line 9 assigns BT01-BT12 to data phase 1 and BT13-BT17 to data phase 2.

Phase3: each native trial's Statics model mass equals exactly one README w/ exo value of the folder's own row (day 1 or day 2), except BT18/BT24; that binds the mass row, and the body mass of the same row. statics_conflict.finding: BT18 folder Statics.csv lists 84.84/87.15 kg models (README BT24 w/ exo day 1/day 2); BT24 folder lists 74.96/75.23 kg (README BT18 day 1/day 2). The two files, the two folders, or the two README rows are swapped; which one is not known.
statics_conflict.existing_data_evidence: GT24-C02 BT24-folder incline trial: lever slope 1.10 with 84.84 kg, i.e. divisor near 75 kg (inside the band for 74.96 kg) if the GT23 lever bias transfers; BT24's README body mass 77.79 kg also fits, so this alone does not decide.
statics_conflict.resolution_plan: E2 plate weight in both folders separates 75 vs 85 kg; E1 confirms the divisor. Then a decision on whether to bind BT18-row body masses to the BT24 folder (and vice versa) or withhold; not raised before data.

c02_divisor_evidence.method: From the GT24-C02 audit only (no new reads). C02 slope = source / (lever-arm moment / m_used) = b * m_used / D, with D the true divisor and b the lever bias (generic talus, foot inertia). For each candidate D, slope * D / m_used should equal b for every trial. b is taken from outside these trials: GT23-C04 rules.ankle_bias_centre_ratio (0.9942), the same lever method calibrated on GT23 trials with known divisors; band +/-4.9 % (GT23-C03 tolerance_v2, reused). One trial per subject, ankle only.
c02_divisor_evidence.assumption: The GT23 lever bias transfers to GT24 (different subjects, OpenSim models and an exoskeleton worn). If it does not, these 6 slopes cannot separate the worn and body divisors: with a free bias per hypothesis both fit 5-6 of 6 (sensitivity_free_bias).
c02_divisor_evidence.reading: If the GT23 lever bias transfers: worn model mass (Statics for Phase3, README w/ exo for Phase1And2) fits 6/6 within the band; README own-row w/ exo fits 5/6 (BT24 folder about +12 %, where its Statics model mass is BT18's README value); body mass w/o exo fits 1/6 (BT24, whose own body mass 77.79 kg lies 3.7 % from its folder model mass 74.96 kg). Without that assumption the slopes do not separate worn from body mass. Preliminary and conditional; the probe (E1, with E3) is the test.

Ankle: GT24-C02 force-plate evidence, dorsiflexion +; README line 91 is wrong for the ankle.

supported_ankle_policy: GT24 ankle (GT24-C02; supersedes the README sign line and gt24-ankle-evidence-ranking.json proposed_mapping). The published ankle_angle_<side> (angle.csv, angle_filt.csv), ankle_angle_<side>_velocity (velocity.csv) and ankle_angle_<side>_moment (moment.csv, moment_filt.csv, moment_filt_bio.csv) are dorsiflexion-positive, with internal moments (plantarflexor negative), as in OpenSim; README line 91 ("ankle plantarflexion is positive") is wrong for the ankle. LocoHub maps them with sign +1 (no negation): ankle_dorsiflexion_angle = rad(ankle_angle); ankle_dorsiflexion_velocity = rad(ankle_angle_velocity); ankle_dorsiflexion_moment and ankle_dorsiflexion_biological_moment = +source x D / m_basis (normalization per D-GT24-C01-1; withheld while D or m_basis is unresolved); ankle_dorsiflexion_assistance_moment = moment_filt - moment_filt_bio (0 in every leg checked; the exoskeleton has no ankle actuator), scaled the same way; ankle powers keep their sign. Published values stay available under source names. Do not adopt prepare_gt24_ankle_fix.py, adopt_gt24_phase_ankle_sign.py or run_gt24_ankle_converter_pilot.py; their negation would make ankle_dorsiflexion_* plantarflexion-positive. Evidence covers forward level, incline and decline walking and heel/toe walking (6 subjects, 12 legs); other tasks use the same coordinate and are not separately tested. Ankle angle zero is the OpenSim model neutral position (not checked).
required_code_changes: gt24_mass_field_policy.normalize_sample: sign table is hip +1, knee -1, ankle -1; the ankle must be +1 (GT24-C02). Blocking for any canonical ankle moment (apply_gt24_participant_normalization_v2 uses it).

probe_plan.status: written, not run (numerical slot held by another agent)
probe_plan.caveat: E1 gives the divisor used to convert torque_interaction before subtraction (bio = net - interaction / D_x). It equals the net-moment divisor only if the authors used the same mass for both. E3 tests that, and E3 carries the same assumption as the C02 re-reading: that the GT23 lever bias transfers to GT24. If E3 cannot confirm D_net = D_x, the net/biological moment divisor stays unresolved even when E1 is exact.

estimators.E1: exact identity interaction = s D_x (moment_filt - moment_filt_bio), plus interaction x velocity = s D_x power_exo (hip, knee, both sides); D_x is the interaction-torque divisor
estimators.E2: plate weight over whole level-walk strides = worn mass
estimators.E3: C02 lever arm in N*m: net ankle moments share the E1 divisor

rules.fixed_at: GT24-C01, before any GT24 data read by this probe

probe_plan.resource_estimate: one worker, one zip member at a time (largest about 5 MB), RLIMIT_AS 1.5 GiB; GT24-C02 read 78 members in 7.3 s at 176 MiB; this reads about 330 members.
probe_plan.launch: Through contributor_tools.guarded_launcher (single job, AGENTS.md prefix): python3 contributor_tools/audit_probes/2026_10_31/probe_gt24_c01_divisors.py pilot
interpretation_rules: E1 exact and equal (0.05 %) to the trial's worn model mass (Statics, or README w/ exo for Phase1And2): D bound for that trial; Phase1And2 repeat-day trials get their mass row from this match.
E1 exact but equal to another value (body mass, another subject, the other day): record as a divisor anomaly; withhold canonical kinetics for that trial pending review.
E1 not exact for both joints/sides: D unbound unless E3 is inside the band of one recorded worn mass that is unique within 8 %; then class "lever_estimate" (not exact).

E3 bias is fixed to the GT23-C04 calibration (0.9942), not re-fitted to the pilot. E3 inside the band of the E1 value: net moments taken to share D_x (conditional on bias transfer). E3 outside: net moments use a different divisor than the interaction subtraction, or the bias does not transfer; stop and report.
E2: worn mass of the person in the folder; BT18/BT24 resolved only if E2 is unique at 2 % and agrees with E1.
If the pilot is all exact, extend E1 (3 members per recording) to all 2,421 recordings as a separate guarded census job; otherwise report and stop.

other_findings: GT25 (same lab, same README template): gt25-normalization-source-review.json keeps an ankle negation from its README; GT24-C02 found the GT24 README ankle line wrong, so GT25-C01 should test its ankle sign independently before adopting the negation.

gt24_source_mass.py refuses to bind Phase3 days from model-mass agreement; this policy binds the README mass row (not a calendar day) through exact equality of two publisher documents, which is source evidence, not inference from trial counters.

readme_mass_spread.note: All README rows, including BT04 (no data)

decision_candidate.question: GT24 participants wore a 6-8 kg exoskeleton. Which mass should LocoHub's standard GT24 moment, power and force columns be per kg of? Published per-kg values will first be converted back with the divisor the authors used, once a probe measures it.

options.label: Leave GT24 kinetics empty
options.consequence: Left out: All standard GT24 moments, powers and body-weight forces. Published per-kg values only under source names; nothing rescaled. Reversible.

options.label: Worn mass (person + exoskeleton)
options.consequence: Left out: BT18/BT24 (146 recordings) until resolved; trials without an established divisor. Published values rescaled from their measured divisor to the worn mass; forces in worn-system weights; values 6-12 % below body-mass values. Reversible.

options.label: Body mass (without exoskeleton)
options.consequence: Left out: As B, plus second-day trials of BT06, BT07, BT13 (first collection): no body mass reported. Published values rescaled from their measured divisor to body mass (× 1.07-1.13 if the measured divisor is the worn mass, × 1 if it is body mass); comparable with datasets without an exoskeleton; published values kept under source names. Reversible.

decision_candidate.options_order: By the normalizing mass: none (withheld), heavier (worn), lighter (body).
decision_candidate.why: LocoHub defines forces in body weights and moments per kg; D-GT23-C03-1 rescaled GT23 to each participant's own mass; the task acceptance forbids substituting exoskeleton model mass for body mass. Source per-kg values stay available, so option B remains recoverable. Cost: second-day trials of three first-collection subjects lose kinetics.
decision_candidate.check: README subject-mass table: every "w/ exo" mass is 6.1-7.8 kg above its "w/o exo" mass.
decision_candidate.cost_of_waiting: GT24 standard kinetic columns cannot be finalized; the divisor probe and all other GT24 work are unaffected.
decision_candidate.queued_until: GT24-C01 divisor probe pilot (E1 with E3) reports; re-check the option wording against it before copying into backlog.json.

limitations: No GT24 time series were read by this task; every divisor statement is preliminary until the probe runs.
C02-derived divisor evidence: 6 trials, one per subject, ankle only, generic talus; the common bias comes from the same trials.
Hip and knee moment signs follow the OpenSim coordinate definition plus encoder checks; no force-plate test of hip/knee moments.
